capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record including bank details
ERP outbound payment run to vendor bank account

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The agent updates vendor bank details whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details,' with no requirement to verify the change out of band. Supplier invoices are attacker-reachable content (in.supplier_invoice, trust_level untrusted), so this line gives an untrusted source direct influence over a sink that controls where future payments go (cap.bank_update).

The only named safeguard before a payment or bank change is 'request approval with a one line summary.' The summary's content and completeness are left entirely to model judgment; nothing structural requires it to disclose the bank account number, the prior value, or that a bank change occurred at all.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The clerk approves or rejects based solely on a one line model-written summary; bank account numbers and change history are not shown (runtime notes). A more capable or hijacked model can write a summary that is accurate about payee and amount while omitting or normalizing a fraudulent bank detail change. At roughly 150 cards/day, scrutiny per card is already low (SAFE-T1403 consent fatigue), so the gate is weaker than a structural, independent control.

governance_refs.note: Human oversight control referenced by ASI09 in the crosswalk.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of new bank details
controls.decay_rationale: Verifying a bank detail change via a phone number already on file, independent of the invoice channel, blocks the path regardless of model behavior: an attacker who only controls invoice text cannot also answer a callback to the vendor's known number.

controls.name: Raw action approval card
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the clerk the actual bank account number, prior value, and payment destination pulled directly from the ERP system of record, rather than a model-written sentence, removes the model's ability to shape what the approver sees, which is what currently makes the gate partially_dependent.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential with maker-checker separation
controls.decay_rationale: Today's ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (runtime notes), so a single bad decision reaches the full blast radius. Scoping the agent's credential to propose-only, with a separate human-held credential required to commit a bank change or payment, narrows the path independent of model behavior.

findings.title: TC9: Summary-gated bank detail change and payment, driven by an untrusted invoice

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled supplier invoice carries new bank account details.
Agent updates vendor bank details based on invoice content alone, per prompt.md:2.
Clerk sees only a one line model summary ('Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187...') with no bank account number or diff, and approves roughly 150 cards/day.
Agent schedules payment to the now attacker-controlled bank account on the due date.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to the underlying model id/version in the platform config (runtime notes state the model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review). Also watch approvals-per-clerk-per-day: already ~150/day, which independently degrades the gate toward the same projected outcome even before a model upgrade (SAFE-T1403 consent fatigue).

evidence.observation: Instruction: 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record,' with no out-of-band verification step named.
Instruction: 'Before any payment or bank change, request approval with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly.'

The card shown is 'Summary: Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521).' It names only payee, amount, invoice, and PO match; no bank account number or change indicator is present.
'The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown.'
'The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day,' indicating low per-card scrutiny.
'The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment,' i.e., credential_scope broad with no least-privilege separation.
'The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review,' directly enabling the model_upgrade forecast trigger.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (callback to a phone number already on file, not one supplied in the invoice) before any bank detail change executes.
Switch the approval card to raw_action review: show the actual bank account number, prior value, and payment destination from the ERP system of record instead of a model-written summary.
Scope the ERP credential to least privilege; require a separate human-held commit credential for bank changes and payments distinct from the agent's propose/read access.
Remove the instruction to update bank details solely because new details appear in an invoice; route any such request to AP staff for manual verification.
Log and alert on bank-detail changes followed by a payment to the same vendor within a short window, and track approvals per reviewer per day to catch approval fatigue.

rating.rationale: One finding was identified: an untrusted supplier invoice can drive a vendor bank-detail change and a subsequent payment schedule, gated only by a clerk approval card that shows a model-written one line summary rather than the raw bank account diff (ASI01, ASI09; TC9 summary-gated irreversible action). Inherent risk is critical: the source is untrusted (in.supplier_invoice) and the sink is S3 (cap.schedule_payment is an explicit spend action with egress of funds; cap.bank_update feeds it). The clerk approval gate is structural but capability_dependence partially_dependent because its approval_review_mode is model_summary, which per rubric section 5 step 2 credits -2 tiers but floors the residual at moderate, giving residual = moderate. No independent structural control (out-of-band verification, raw action review, or scoped credential) is currently in place to narrow or sever the path further. Under the model_upgrade trigger -- already anticipated, since runtime notes state the model upgrades with the platform with no separate review -- the approval gate's partially_dependent credit is defeated and the finding reverts to its inherent tier of critical. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.clerk_approval.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, the approval card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; capability action semantics and credential scope are inferred from the runtime notes' plain-language description, so confidence on exact classification detail is medium even though confidence on the overall attack path is high.
No logging, audit, or anomaly-detection control was described in the artifacts; detective controls are assumed absent rather than verified absent.
